 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 25-02-2024 at about 18:30:00., the petitioner was riding Scooter bearing No.KA-12-C-2386 along with pillion rider ie., her husband by name Pranit Dilip Gujar who is petitioner in MVC No.5074/2025 on Kushalnagara.

When they reached near Capital village, Kadagadalu village, Madikeri Tq, Kodagu, at that time the driver of car bearing No.KA-05-Z-9812 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle, result of which, the petitioner and her husband fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to District Hospital,
Madikeri wherein admitted as an inpatient from 25-02- 2024 to 26-02-2024 and then she was shifted to Mazumdar Shaw Medical Centre, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient from 26-02-2025 to 28-02- 2024.
As per the advice of doctor, the petitioner continuing follow up treatment.

So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
3.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
She was aged about 35 years.
She was giving tuition in the house on part time and earning sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Car bearing No.KA-05-Z-9812 has remained absent.
Hence, he was placed ex-parte.

5. The Respondent no.2 /the insurer of Car bearing No.KA-05-Z-9812 has filed written statement and disputed the coverage of Insurance policy as on the date of accident and submitted that the policy particulars furnished by the petitioner is policy bearing No.0706033122P10460512 and same Rina Pranit Gujar vs Chandrashekar C C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119577787/
2 was valid from 19-08-2022 to 18-08-2023 and the policy was not in existence during the period of accident.

sentences.text: In view of the non -existence of the policy of insurance issued in respect of Maruthi Omni car as on the date of accident, the respondent no.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, she has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 25-02-2024 at about 18:30:00 near Capital village, Kadagadulu village, Madikeri Tq, Kodagu, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-Z-9812?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. The petitioner got examined herself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as P.W.2 and PW.3 and marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.
The respondent no.2 has examined its Administrative Officer as Rw.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3:
Issue No.1:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed her affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 25-02-2024 at about 18:30:00., when the petitioner was riding Scooter bearing No.KA-12-C-2386 along with pillion rider ie., her husband by name Pranit Dilip Gujar who is petitioner in MVC No.5074/2025 on Kushalnagara and when they reached near Capital village, Kadagadalu village,
Madikeri Tq, Kodagu at that time the driver of car bearing No.KA-05-Z-9812 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle,
result of which, the she and her husband fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment Rina Pranit Gujar vs Chandrashekar C C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119577787/
3 etc.
11.

sentences.text:
In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 in has relied upon Ex.P6 to 16 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, crime details form, seizer mahazar, notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, IMV report, AIR report, charge sheet, RC, Insurance policy, permit, DL of petitioner etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by petitioner, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0040/2024 by Madikeri Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and U/Sec.134 (a&b) of MV Act.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC and U/Sec.187 of MV Act.
13.

So far as the contention taken by the petitioner as to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the spot mahazar and sketch so also other document and the evidence of PW.1 is perused, at the time of accident the petitioner along with her husband was proceeding towards Madikeri through Chettalli road.
The offending vehicle was proceeding from opposite direction ie., from Madikeri towards Chettalli.
The width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 20 feet.
The accident in question has occurred on the extreme left side of Chettalli - Madikeri road.

It clearly reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle who was driving from Madikeri side towards Chettalli took his vehicle on the extreme right side of the road by encroaching nearly 15 feet road and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner.
Had the driver driven his vehicle on the left side of Madikeri - Chettalli road this accident would not have occurred.
Hence, in the accident the petitioner has not contributed any amount of negligence.

Though the respondent no.2 has denied the manner of accident and submitted that the negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle is the cause for the accident but they have not examined the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondent no.1 is the driver/ owner of the offending vehicle.
He remained ex-parte.
If really the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the rider of the two wheeler, then nothing prevented the respondent no.1 from giving evidence to that effect.

Hence,
the materials placed on record and un-rebutted version of the PW.1 which supports the case of the petitioner.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are at Ex.P1 and P2.

On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken primary treatment at District Hospital Madikeri on 25-02-2024 and then she was shifted to Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient from 26-02-2024 to 28-02-2024 for a period of 3 days.
As per the wound certificate petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury no.1 is simple in nature and injury no.2 is grievous in nature.
15. Dr. S A Somashekara - Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore is examined as Pw-2 and through him OPD and x-ray are marked as Ex.P23 and Ex.P24.
The PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 29-11-2024, clinically and radiologically for assessment of disability.

PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent disability of right lower limb at 26%

4 and to the whole body at 13%.

sentences.text: 16. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, the PW.2 has not given treatment to the petitioner and except assessing disability, at no point of time he had given treatment to the petitioner.

As observed supra, the petitioner has assessed the disability of petitioner on right lower limb at 26%
and on whole body at 13%.

As per the judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk, the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3rd of the particular limb.

entities.text: 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If that being the case the PW.2 ought to have assessed the disability on whole body at 12%.
But this court even hesitate to take the disability at 12% for the reason of the evidence given by PW.2.
Hence, this court inclines to assess the disability of the petitioner at 10% instead of 12% on whole body.
17. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
18. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering.
19. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, she has produced medical bills for Rs.2,15,743/- as per Ex.P3.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,15,743/- under the head medical expenses.
20. It is stated that petitioner was doing tuition in house on part time and earning sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- p.m.
21.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 3 days as an inpatient in Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bangalore.
Hence, it is reasonable to hold that period of 3 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this Tribunal takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15,000/- p.m for 3 months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.45,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
22. From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, Bangalore.

For 2 days of hospitalization requires an attendant,
was traveled to hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
23. It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident she was aged about 35 years.
In this regard, she has produced his Aadhaar card/Ex.P5 which shows her date of birth as 27-04-1989.

As Rina Pranit Gujar vs Chandrashekar C C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119577787/
5

sentences.text: the accident took place in the year 2024, the petitioner was aged about 35 years as on the date of accident.

24. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,000/- p.m and if 10% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 35 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 is '16".
So by applying the multiplier '16' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.2,88,000/- (i.e., 15,000/- x 10% x 16 x12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,88,000/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
25. The petitioner at her age of 35 years has suffered grievous injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

Thus, the Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Under the Heads Amount No. (in Rupees )
1 . Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 1,00,000/-

2. Medical expenses Rs. 2,15,743/-
 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 45,000/-
 laid up period

4 . Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food

5. Future Loss of Income Rs. 2,88,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities and Rs. 30,000/-
 discomforts

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,98,743/- (Rupees Six Lakh Ninety Eight Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Three only).
26.
As regarding liability is concerned, respondent no.2 in its written statement and in its evidence has seriously disputed the issuance of policy in respect of the offending vehicle.

It is categorically submitted by the respondent no.2 that they have issued policy in respect of the offending vehicle valid from 19-08-2022 to 18-08- 2023 and since the accident in question has occurred on 25-02-2024, as on the date of accident insurance policy was not in force, hence, they are not liable to pay the compensation.
27.

Per contra, it is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that respondent no.2 company itself has issued policy number mentioned in the petition through their agent and now in order to escape from the liability they are falsely stating so.

In order to justify the said contention,
the petitioner has produced the Insurance policy as per Ex.P14 and also examined the investigating officer as PW.3.
The PW.3 who is the investigating officer in Cr No.40/2024 has deposed that in the Ex.P11 ie., Accident Information Report it is mentioned that the policy was in force from 23-03-2023 to 22-03-2024.

It is further deposed by PW.3 that in the reply notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Rina Pranit Gujar vs Chandrashekar C C on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119577787/
6 Act the owner has stated that the policy in respect of the offending vehicle was issued from the respondent no.2 and that during the course of investigation he has received copy of the insurance policy from the respondent no.1 and as per the Ex.P14, the policy was in force from 24-08-2023 to 23-08-2024.

entities.text: IMV Rina Pranit Gujar vs Chandrashekar C C
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is admitted by PW.3 that in the Ex.P14 there is mention about issuance of policy on 17-08-2022.
The PW.3 voluntarily deposed that alleging that, 1st respondent has created Insurance policy, criminal case is registered in Cr No. 169/2024 and the investigation is in progress.
The PW.3 has produced during his cross examination the FIR copy as per Ex.R1 in MVC No. 5074/2024 registered against the respondent no.1 for creation of Insurance policy.

Though the PW.3 in his evidence has deposed that Ex.P14 was issued by the authorized agent of the respondent no.2 and that even against the alleged authorized agent by name Madhan and Shweth criminal case is registered and investigation is in progress but deposed that there is no document to evidence the said fact and admitted that as per Ex.R1 criminal case is registered only against the respondent no.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle.
28.
Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here Ex.P14 relied by the petitioner and Ex.R2 relied by the respondent no.2.
If both Ex.P14 and Ex.R2 are carefully perused, in both the documents the date of issuance of policy is mentioned as 17-08-2022.
Having noted in Ex.P14 that policy was issued on 17-08-2022 but the validity period of said policy is mentioned as from 24-08-2023 to 23-08-2024.
If really, policy was in force from 24-08-2023 to 23-08-2024, then the question of issuance of policy on 17-08-2022 would not arise.

If Ex.R2 is perused, wherein while mentioning the date of issuance of policy on 17-08-2022 , the validity period of policy is shown as from 19-08-2022 to 18-08-2023.
29.

It is vehemently argued by the Learned counsel for petitioner that the authorized agent of the respondent no.2 themselves have issued Ex.P14 hence when respondent no.2 through its authorized agent has issued Ex.P14, even if any fraud is committed by the authorized agent, for which respondent no.1 can not be held liable.
30. It is relevant to state here that respondent no.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle has remained absent.

If really, respondent no.1 has taken insurance policy from the authorized agent of the respondent no.2 covering the period 24-08-2023 to 23- 08-2024 as depicted in the Ex.P14 and if really no fraud has been played by him, then it is for the respondent no.1 to say on the said material fact.
The petitioner is totally stranger to the alleged contract between the respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 so far as Insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle is concerned.
The petitioner could have summoned the respondent no.1 in support of his contention.

When respondent no.1 himself has remained silent and he has not spoken anything about the validity of Ex.P14 and the existence of Insurance policy on the date of accident, under such circumstances by relying upon the date of issuance of policy mentioned in the Ex.P14 coupled with Ex.R2 wherein the validity period of Insurance policy is clearly mentioned as 19-08-2022 to 18-08-2023 which does not cover the risk as on the date of accident, under such circumstances it can be said that there was no contract between the respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 so far as offending vehicle is concerned.
When Insurance policy itself was not in force as on the date of accident, the question of respondent no.2 paying compensation does not arise.

7 31.

sentences.text:
The Learned counsel for 2nd respondent has relied upon the judgment reported in ILR 1997 Kar 1061 between The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs., N S Devaraja & Ors., wherein it was observed that "when the Insurance company stated in its objection statement that the vehicle was not insured, the burden of proving that the vehicle was insurer lay either with the complainant or the owner of vehicle.
32.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs., N S Devaraja & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In ILR 1997 Kar 1980 between The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Chikkegowda & ors., in which it was observed that " in cases where Insurance company disputes its liability on the ground that Insurance particulars are not given, it is duty of the claimants or the owners of the vehicle to furnish all such particulars to show that the offending vehicle was insured on the relevant date.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Chikkegowda & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not for the Insurance company to prove that the vehicle is not insured with them.

33. In ILR 2016 Kar 2014 between The Divisional Manager, M/s The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs.
J.M Somnath & Anr.

entities.text:
Divisional Manager, M/s The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs.
J.M Somnath & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also the grievance of insurance company was that offending vehicle was not insured with him.
In the said case, the petitioner has not produced material document to prove that the offending vehicle was insured with the insurance company.
Under the given set of fact it was held that "it is settled law that a party to a judicial proceeding cannot be expected to prove the negative.

The claimant having contended that offending vehicle was insured with the appellate/insurer company was expected to prove his case either by producing the insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle or by adducing cogent evidence to that effect.
It was held that the approach of the Tribunal that the insurance company has not proved that offending vehicle was not insured with them is unknown to law of evidence.

The Hon'ble High Court reversed the finding given by the Tribunal by fastening liability on the owner and insurer of the vehicle to pay the compensation jointly and severally and ordered the owner to pay the compensation.

34. The observation made in the aforesaid rulings is aptly applicable to the case in hand as in the instant case also the petitioner has failed to prove that as on the date of accident the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no.1.
Further respondent no.1 has remained silent.

Even though there was no obligation on the part of the respondent no.2 to prove the fact of non existence of policy in spite of that the respondent no.2 by producing Ex.R2 to Ex.R4 has proved the defence taken by it.
If Ex.R3 and Ex.R4 is perused, on 08-10- 2024 notice was issued to the respondent no.1 to produce Insurance particulars and such other documents.

Though the notice issued through RPAD was served to the respondent no.1 but he failed to appear before the court or appear before the Insurance company and failed to produce particulars of Insurance policy.
Hence, at the cost of repetition it can be said that as on the date of accident the insurance policy was not in force.

Hence,
the insurance company is exonerated from liability and liability is fastened only against the owner of the vehicle.

The owner of offending vehicle ie., respondent no.1 is directed to pay the compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
35. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,98,743/- (Rupees Six Lakh Ninety Eight Thousand Seven Hundred Forty Three only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
